processing: Darjeeling orthodox processing as is usual for the district: withered, rolled, oxidised and fired, with lighter oxidation in spring.
harvest_season: As usual in Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush in early summer, then monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, twisted olive-and-brown leaf with pale tips, darker in summer lots.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in spring, amber in summer and autumn.
appearance_wet: Soft green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner later.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this garden's own cup. Darjeelings of this type run floral and brisk in spring, fruitier and fuller in summer.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for first flush and shorten the steep if it turns sharp.

vintage_note: Usual for Darjeeling: sold by year and flush, with lot numbers and grades on single-estate tea. First flush is best within about a year. Because replanting here is fairly recent, the year on the lot is worth noting.
description:
Rohini is a garden in the Kurseong block of Darjeeling district, unusual because it is young by local standards. Most famous Darjeeling gardens date from the colonial era; Rohini is one of only eight new gardens developed in India after independence.

Processing details specific to the garden are scarce, so expect the district's orthodox pattern: light oxidation in spring, more in summer.

Brew it like other Darjeelings, cooler for spring lots. There is no well-documented house style to look for, so taste the lot rather than the reputation.

For contrast, try it next to a Kurseong garden with a far older planting history and see whether the bush age shows in your cup.
history:
Rohini was first planted in 1955, then closed in 1962. It stayed shut until around the end of the twentieth century, when the Saria family took it over and began replanting.

That long gap makes its current bushes much younger than those of most of its neighbours in the Darjeeling hills.
